## Why

**Every codex keepalive run across the fleet is currently inert.** The agent executes no
commands at all, and reports the result as a successful turn.

codex's `workspace-write` sandbox shells out to bubblewrap, which unshares the network
namespace and then brings up loopback. Bringing up `lo` requires `CAP_NET_ADMIN` inside that
namespace, and Ubuntu 24.04+ runner images ship
`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`, which withholds it. Every shell command dies
before it runs:

```
bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted
```

This is a known upstream regression: openai/codex#14719, #15982, #17337, #19235.

Measured 2026-09-13 by downloading the `codex-output-*` artifacts. From
`stranske/Doc-Lineage` #23:

```
Blocked by the execution environment: shell commands fail before running with
`bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted`, including a retry without
login-shell initialization. I couldn't inspect files, implement changes, run Black/tests,
or commit. No tasks were marked complete.
```

and the session analysis for that run: `"command_count": 0, "file_change_count": 0`,
`"blocked_tasks"` listing all six.

**The reason this went unnoticed for so long is the reporting, not the failure.** codex exits
0, so the keepalive loop records `Status: ✅ Success`, the dispatch debounce writes a terminal
`completed` record, and the PR goes quiet looking healthy. `stranske/Ready` #569 appears
productive only because its commits come from the Claude autofix path; its codex runs are
blocked identically. The three new repos have no `CLAUDE_AUTH_JSON`, so they have no working
agent at all — which is why they produce bootstrap PRs and then nothing.

## Non-goals

- Waiting for the upstream fix. The fleet is inert now.
- Weakening filesystem confinement. `workspace-write` stays.

## Tasks

- [ ] Restore the capability the sandbox needs where possible: best-effort
      `sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0` before invoking codex.
      This keeps the sandbox exactly as designed.
- [ ] Fallback when that is not permitted: retry the same model once with
      `--config sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true`, which makes bwrap share the host
      network namespace instead of unsharing it, so the loopback setup never happens.
- [ ] Stop reporting a sandbox that never started as a successful run. A `bwrap:` line in the
      session output must force a non-zero exit so the loop's error handling engages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A codex keepalive run in a consumer repo executes shell commands and produces a commit.
- [ ] A run whose sandbox fails to start reports a failure, not a success.

## Implementation notes

`.github/workflows/reusable-codex-run.yml`, the step that builds and runs the `codex exec`
command. The third task matters independently of the first two: it is the reporting half of
the latch described in #3433 — a run that did nothing must not be able to write a terminal
completion record.

Consumer execution is also observed: Ready PR #569 keepalive work log records Codex commits baf08877b970f9dc4d4a90b7f5e7545d57fe9b02 at 04:12 UTC and f96303e98878e291ddeefea0da97689f6dc19715 at 04:20 UTC on September 14.
